corrected_value.authors: Isoni, Andrea, Loomes, Graham, Sugden, Robert
corrected_value.title: The willingness to pay–willingness to accept gap, the “Endowment Effect,” subject misconceptions, and experimental procedures for eliciting valuations: comment.

decisions.quote:
In line with PZ and ILS, we find a strong WTP–WTA gap in the lottery tasks. In contrast to PZ and ILS, however, the gap
does not disappear in the main task where subjects submit their WTA or WTP for a mug (or USB stick).
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. The paper explicitly states that it replicates the computerized experiments of both Plott and Zeiler (2005; PZ) and Isoni, Loomes, and Sugden (2011; ILS) as closely as possible (Sections 1 and 2) and directly compares its empirical results against both PZ and ILS on the paid lottery tasks and the classic mug valuation task (Section 3.1, concluding 'Thus, we are not able to replicate the results on the valuations of mugs by PZ and ILS.'). Shipped row input_row_index 2519 represents only Plott and Zeiler (2005, doi 10.1257/0002828054201387). Isoni, Loomes, and Sugden (2011), published in American Economic Review 101, 991-1011, is an independent study by different authors reporting new computerized experiments rather than an alternate report of Plott and Zeiler (2005), so it is a genuinely absent original target.
